title: Dormancy and Courtesy Refund Parameters for Savings and Money Market Accounts
content:
Four per-tier parameters govern how long an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts may sit without customer-initiated activity before it is classified dormant, what it is charged each cycle while dormant, how many courtesy fee refunds a customer may receive across all of their savings accounts in a rolling 365 days, and how recently a fee must have posted to be eligible for a courtesy refund.

| Tier | Months without customer-initiated activity before dormancy | Dormant account fee per cycle | Courtesy refunds in a rolling 365 days | Courtesy refund window after the fee posted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Starter Savings | 24 calendar months | 0.00 USD | 1 | 60 calendar days |
| Statement Savings | 24 calendar months | 3.00 USD | 1 | 60 calendar days |
| Goal Builder Savings | 24 calendar months | 0.00 USD | 1 | 60 calendar days |
| Money Market Account | 24 calendar months | 5.00 USD | 2 | 60 calendar days |
| Premier Money Market | 24 calendar months | 5.00 USD | 3 | 90 calendar days |
| Private Client Money Market | 36 calendar months | 0.00 USD | 6 | 120 calendar days |

### Notes on the parameters

The dormancy parameter is 24 calendar months on five tiers; Private Client Money Market alone carries 36 calendar months. The dormant account fee is charged per statement cycle while the account is dormant and never takes the balance below zero; it is 0.00 USD on Starter Savings, Goal Builder Savings and Private Client Money Market.

The courtesy refund count is a customer-level figure: it counts refunded fees across all of that customer's savings accounts, not per account. It widens with the tier, from 1 on the three savings tiers to 6 on Private Client Money Market. The courtesy window widens with it, from 60 calendar days to 120.
